newsitem.title: USA: EMU stability pact not a problem for Italy -Ciampi.
newsitem.headline: EMU stability pact not a problem for Italy -Ciampi.

text.p: The European monetary union stability pact recently approved at the EU summit in Amsterdam should not create any difficulties for Italy, Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi said.
Ciampi was replying to reporters' questions after his arrival in Denver for the Group of Seven (G7) summit.
He was asked if Europe's plans to create a stable currency union with lasting fiscal austerity would be a problem for Italy.

Ciampi replied, "No, because we we will easily reach the three percent (deficit/GDP EMU goal) in 1997 and this will trigger a virtuous cicle which will allow us to reduce the cost of public debt," he said.

Asked to comment on the fact that the Bank of Italy had not yet cut its key 6.75 percent discount rate, a move widely expected in financial markets, Ciampi said "I'm interested in market rates. Rates are falling," he said.
"I don't see why the spread over German rates, which is now around 130 basis points, should not fall to that of Spanish levels, of 65 basis points," he added.
He said the main factor preventing the Italy/Germany differential falling even further below this target was the "volume of (Italian) public debt."
